worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $f(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{g(t)}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t) & =\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t) \\  & =\frac{{\int }_{0}^{1}7t\cdot (t-2)\,\text{d}t}{{\int }_{0}^{1}(t-2)^{2}\,\text{d}t}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =\frac{{\int }_{0}^{1}(7{t}^{2}-14t)\,\text{d}t}{{\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}-4t+4)\,\text{d}t}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =\frac{[\frac{7}{3}{t}^{3}-7{t}^{2}]_{0}^{1}}{[\frac{1}{3}{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+4t]_{0}^{1}}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{14}{3})}{(\frac{7}{3})}\cdot (t-2) \\  & =-2t+4.\end{aligned}
$$

The distance between $f(t)=7t$ and the subspace spanned by $g(t)=t-2$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖f(t)-{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t)‖ \\  & =‖7t-(-2t+4)‖ \\  & =‖9t-4‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨9t-4,9t-4⟩}\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨9t-4,9t-4⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9t-4)\cdot (9t-4)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(9t-4)^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(81{t}^{2}-72t+16)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(27{t}^{3}-36{t}^{2}+16)\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{7}.$
